findings.evidence: "A unit test is a small piece of code that checks that another piece of code works. A test suite is a collection of tests... Mocking replaces a dependency with a fake one. Coverage tells you how much of the code ran."
findings.fix: The model reliably knows what unit tests, suites, mocking and coverage are: delete this Background section and record the removal

findings.evidence: "Create a file named `test_something.py`. Import the module. Write a function that starts with `test_`. Use `assert` to compare values."
findings.fix: Step-by-step pytest tutorial the model already knows: delete the section and record the removal; keep only repo-specific conventions

findings.evidence: Fifteen near-identical subsections ("### unit tests" through "### payment tests"), each repeating "Repeat the arrange, act and assert pattern for every <kind> test you write." with a trivial placeholder example — ~197 of 231 lines restate one naming rule the model can derive
findings.fix: Collapse to one rule ("Name tests test_<kind>_<behavior> in tests/<kind>/ for kind in unit, integration, api, cli, database, auth, billing, search, upload, export, email, cache, queue, payment") plus one example, and move the full per-kind detail into a skill this plugin bundles, preloaded via skills:

findings.evidence: "6. Do your best and make sure everything works." — the procedure list carries no thinking framework and no domain sequence beyond run/fix genericities
findings.fix: Replace generic steps 5-6 with the reasoning an expert applies, e.g. "before fixing, ask whether the intended behavior changed (fix the test) or the code regressed (fix the code); order: reproduce, diagnose, fix, re-run the targeted tests"

findings.evidence: File mixes a definitions tutorial (line 10), a pytest tutorial (line 17), a contradictory 6-step list (line 23) and a padded reference (line 35) — no coherent pattern for a testing agent
findings.fix: Restructure as a short process agent: role, one naming rule, an ordered test workflow with checkpoints; delete the tutorials (record removals) and split the reference to a bundled skill

findings.evidence: "4. Fix the code or the test, whichever is easier. Delete tests that get in the way." — enshrines the cardinal anti-pattern of deleting failing tests to go green
findings.fix: Replace with a NEVER with reason: "NEVER delete or skip a failing test to make the suite pass; decide code-vs-test from whether the intended behavior changed, and only remove tests that duplicate coverage or test deleted behavior, saying why"

findings.evidence: "5. Be careful, think about edge cases and write good tests." — vague warning, no specific edge cases or landmines
findings.fix: List concrete cases this repo's tests must cover (empty input, boundary values, error paths, network/db fixtures) instead of the generic admonition

findings.evidence: Frontmatter (lines 1-6) carries name, permissionMode, tools and model but no description — the agent cannot be routed to
findings.fix: Add a description: "Writes and fixes this repository's tests: names tests test_<kind>_<behavior> under tests/<kind>/ (unit, integration, api, cli, database, auth, billing, search, upload, export, email, cache, queue, payment), diagnoses failures, and decides code-vs-test fixes. Use when asked to add, update, debug or reorganize tests, when a suite fails after a change, or when the user mentions pytest, mocking, coverage or flaky tests, even without the word 'test'. Not for running CI pipelines or writing benchmarks."

findings.evidence: "permissionMode: bypassPermissions" — this agent ships in a plugin, where the host ignores permissionMode
findings.fix: Remove the field from the agent frontmatter; if bypass permissions is required, configure it at plugin/session level instead

findings.evidence: "follow the steps in the section \"Recovery\"" — no Recovery section exists anywhere in the file; the reference does not resolve
findings.fix: Either add a "## Recovery" section holding the failure-recovery steps, or rewrite step 3 to point at steps that exist

findings.evidence: 231-line agent with no skills: preload; "## Test naming reference" alone spans lines 35-231 with nothing split out of the body
findings.fix: Move the per-kind naming rules into a bundled skill preloaded via skills:, keeping routing and the workflow in the agent file (or collapse the repetition to bring the file under 200 lines)

findings.evidence: "Fix the code or the test, whichever is easier." — menu of equal options with no default and no criteria for a decision with real consequences
findings.fix: Give a default with an escape hatch: "Default to fixing the code when the failure reproduces in the changed behavior; fix the test only when the intended contract changed — state which and why"

findings.evidence: The Instructions never state when the task is done ("6. Do your best and make sure everything works." is not a completion condition) and no output format is defined
findings.fix: Add a sentence such as: "Done when the targeted tests pass and any full-suite run you made is green; report in a list: tests added, fixed or deleted, the failing-to-passing change, and the final pytest summary line"

findings.evidence: "1. Always run the whole test suite before you change anything." directly contradicts "2. Never run the whole test suite, because it is slow; run only the test file that you changed." — the branch cannot resolve
findings.fix: Merge into one conditional rule, e.g. "Run the tests covering the code you are about to change before editing; run the full suite before declaring the task done"

findings.evidence: "go on to step 12." — the numbered list ends at step 6; following step 3's branch reaches no outcome
findings.fix: Renumber step 3 to an existing step (e.g. "then continue with step 4") or add the missing steps 7-12 including the recovery path
